newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Bank Qld against Suncorp stake tranfer.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Bank Qld against Suncorp stake tranfer.

text.p: The Bank of Queensland Ltd said on Friday it believed the transfer of Suncorp Insurance and Finance's 44 percent stake in the bank to Metway Bank Ltd was undesirable.
On Thursday, the Bank of Queensland said it would hold talks with the Queensland state government about the future of the Suncorp stake.

This follows the passing in the Queensland parliament of a bill facilitating a previously announced merger proposal between Suncorp, the Queenland Industry and Development Corporation (QIDC) and Metway.
The merger plan includes a proposal that Suncorp's shares in Bank of Queensland be transferred to Metway.

However, the merger legislation was amended to ensure that the Suncorp stake would not be transferred under the merger terms unless Bank of Queensland shareholders approve the transfer at a meeting where Metway and Suncorp cannot vote.

The proposed merger follows a bidding battle in late June with St George Bank Ltd for Metway which was won by the Queensland government after it raised its offer to A$4.80 per share, topping St George's A$4.77 bid.

Bank of Queensland said the share transfer to Metway was undesirable because Metway was a competitor in many areas of business and there would be problems with board representation on Bank of Queensland's board.
Bank of Queensland also said that the transfer would be against Reserve Bank and Federal Treasury policy for one Australian licensed bank to hold 44.4 percent of another.
"We intend to continue discussions with the government about the future of this shareholding, in the interests of all the bank's shareholders and its customers and staff," the bank said.
